title: Finite etale local polynomial lifts of residue splitting fields
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ an integral finite-type $k$-scheme. Let $s\in S$ and let $E\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, where $F=\kappa(s)$, be finite etale, with $E$ possibly empty. Put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $K=k(S)$. Then $R$ is a Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$ and residue field $F$. There exist a finite set $B$, finite separable field extensions $F_b/F$, an $F$-algebra isomorphism $\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)\cong\prod_{b\in B}F_b$, a finite Galois extension $L/F$ with $F$-embeddings $F_b\hookrightarrow L$, and an element $\alpha\in L$ generating $L/F$. If $q\in F[T]$ is the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha$, then $q$ is separable of degree $d\ge1$ and $F[T]/(q)\cong L$. There exists a monic $f\in R[T]$ of degree $d$ reducing to $q$ such that $C=R[T]/(f)$ is finite free of rank $d$ with basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{d-1}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is finite etale. Its closed fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and there are a nonempty finite set $A$, finite separable extensions $K_a/K$, and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $K[T]/(f)\cong\prod_{a\in A}K_a$. When $E$ is empty one may take $B=\varnothing$, $L=F$, $\alpha=0$, $q=T$ and $f=T$.

Field extensions and separability use [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; finite Galois means finite-dimensional, separable and normal, where normal means that every minimal polynomial splits into linear factors. Integral scheme, finite type, residue field, function field, finite morphism, etaleness, polynomial ring and Noetherian ring use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Finite free with the displayed basis means that its elements are uniquely sums of scalar multiples of those basis elements. The product over an empty set is the zero ring.

proof.text: The ring $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a one-point Noetherian scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to obtain that $S$ is Noetherian. By [pqf-def-locnoeth], choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $s$ with $D$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], its stalk at $s$ is $D_{\mathfrak p}$, where $\mathfrak p$ represents $s$; the stalk on $U$ is the stalk on $S$, since their neighbourhood systems at $s$ agree after intersection with $U$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $R$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], $R$ is a domain with fraction field $K$. The local ring and residue field in [def-weil-residue-field] give the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$ and $F=R/\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); properties.tex Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); integral-scheme fraction-field identifications

proof.text: Since the given map $E\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is finite, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] makes $E$ affine, say $E=\operatorname{Spec}D_E$, with $D_E=\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The map is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] gives $D_E\cong\prod_{b\in B}F_b$ for a finite set $B$ and finite separable $F_b/F$. This theorem explicitly permits the zero algebra and the empty product.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); morphisms.tex Tag 01WH (definition-integral) for finiteness and affineness

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the finite family $(F_b/F)$, after indexing $B$ by $\{1,\ldots,|B|\}$. It gives a finite separable normal extension $L/F$ and $F$-algebra maps $F_b\to L$. Each map is injective: its kernel is an ideal of a field and cannot contain $1$, because $1$ maps to $1\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element] to $L/F$ to choose $\alpha$ with $L=F(\alpha)$. By [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], the minimal polynomial $q$ of $\alpha$ is monic and separable. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], its degree $d$ is at least one and evaluation at $\alpha$ gives $F[T]/(q)\cong F(\alpha)=L$.

source.place: Tags 09DT (lemma-normal-closure) and 0EXM (lemma-normal-closure-galois), with the primitive-element construction used in algebra.tex Tag 00UD

proof.text: Write $q=T^d+\sum_{i<d}\bar a_iT^i$. The residue map $R\to R/\mathfrak m=F$ is surjective, so choose $a_i\in R$ lifting each $\bar a_i$ and put $f=T^d+\sum_{i<d}a_iT^i$. Its leading coefficient is exactly $1$, so $f$ is monic of degree $d$ and reduces to $q$. Put $C=R[T]/(f)$ and let $t$ be the class of $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $C$ has the displayed basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$ and $C/\mathfrak m C\cong F[T]/(q)\cong L$.

source.place: Tag 00UD (lemma-make-etale-map-prescribed-residue-field), coefficient lifting with R already local; monic division as in the proof of Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian)

proof.text: By [def-pc-separable-polynomial], choose $U,V\in F[T]$ with $Uq+Vq'=1$. Coefficientwise lifting gives $\widetilde U,\widetilde V\in R[T]$. Differentiation commutes with reduction by its coefficient formula. Consequently, for $u=f'(t)\in C$, the element $1-\widetilde V(t)u$ lies in $\mathfrak m C$. Set $M=C/uC$, viewed as an $R$-module. The images of the $d$ power-basis elements of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] generate $M$. The identity just obtained implies $C=uC+\mathfrak m C$: multiply it by each $c\in C$. Hence $M=\mathfrak m M$. Because $R$ is local, its Jacobson radical, the intersection of its maximal ideals, is its unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] with $I=\mathfrak m$ and this finite module $M$; it gives $M=0$. Thus $uC=C$, so $uv=1$ for some $v\in C$: the lifted derivative is a unit in $C$.

source.place: Tag 00UD, derivative inversion; Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2), applied to C/f′(t)C to justify that no localization of C is needed

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] with $S=R$ and $Q=f$ to the etale algebra $C'=R[T][Y]/(f,Yf'-1)$. The map $C'\to C$ sends $T$ to $t$ and $Y$ to $u^{-1}$. Conversely $C\to C'$ sends $t$ to the class of $T$. Their composites fix $t$ and every scalar; the composite on $C'$ also fixes $Y$, since $Y$ and the image of $u^{-1}$ are both inverses of $f'(T)$. Thus $C\cong C'$ over $R$, and $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale. It is finite in the sense of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R_V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ be any affine open. Its preimage in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is the open subscheme $V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}C$, which [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_V\otimes_RC)$. So the morphism is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $R_V\otimes_RC$ is generated as an $R_V$-module by the elements $1\otimes t^i$ ($0\le i<d$), the images of the power basis of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free].

source.place: Tag 00UC (lemma-standard-etale), part (1), and Tag 00UD; specialization when f′ is already a unit in the monic quotient

proof.text: For any $R$-algebra $H$, the maps on generators $h\otimes[p(T)]\mapsto h[p(T)]$ and $[T]\mapsto1\otimes t$ give mutually inverse $H$-algebra maps $H\otimes_R C\cong H[T]/(f_H)$: both composites fix $H$ and the class of $T$, which generate these algebras, and the relation $f$ vanishes on both sides. For $H=F$ this is the reduction isomorphism of step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the closed fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}L$. For $H=K$, the same node identifies the generic fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(K[T]/(f_K))$. It is etale over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] gives a finite product $\prod_{a\in A}K_a$ with each $K_a/K$ finite separable. The index set $A$ is nonempty: the monic polynomial $f_K$ has degree $d\ge1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives a basis with $d$ elements over the nonzero field $K$, whereas the empty product is the zero algebra.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); morphisms.tex Tag 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale); affine tensor presentation and monic division

proof.text: If $E$ is empty, its section ring is the zero ring, so take $B=\varnothing$. Take the identity extension $L=F$, $\alpha=0$, $q=T$ and $f=T$. Every element of $F$ has a degree-one minimal polynomial over $F$, which splits and is separable, so the identity extension is finite Galois. Evaluation at $0$ identifies both $F[T]/(T)$ with $F$ and $R[T]/(T)$ with $R$. The power basis is $(1)$ and $q'=f'=1$. The constructions above therefore apply with $d=1$, and the generic product may be the one-factor product $K$ itself.
